newsitem.title: USA: CoreStates willing to reimburse -- issuers.
newsitem.headline: CoreStates willing to reimburse -- issuers.

text.p: CoreStates Capital Markets, a unit of CoreStates Financial Corp, has informed municipalities that it will reimburse them for any financial losses resulting from a federal probe into possible yield burning by Meridian Capital Markets, which CoreStates acquired last year, municipal officials said Friday.
"We've been contacted by CoreStates," Robert Kreitz, solicitor for Pennsylvania's Oley Valley School District and a partner with Rhoda, Stoudt & Bradley, said in a telephone interview.
"They indicated that if losses were found to occur they would reimburse us," Kreitz said, in describing the highly unusual February 21 letter to municipalities from the firm.

As reported by Reuters March 12, the Securities and Exchange Commission has subpoenaed Allentown, Whitehall Township and other Pennsylvania authorities to determine if yield burning occurred in as many as 25 recent refunding deals.
CoreStates would not comment on whether it plans to reimburse localities.
An SEC official was unavailable for comment.

The $1.3 trillion municipal bond market has been rocked by allegations that bond underwriters overcharge issuers for U.S. Treasuries bought in the open market and used in bond refinancing transactions, a practice dubbed yield burning.

Jack Meyers, assistant executive for Whitehall Township told Reuters on March 12 that the SEC's Philadelphia office requested documents in February for a $4.94 million bond refunding handled in 1993 by Meridian.
Meyers said that CoreStates also promised his township that it would reimburse it if the township is cited by regulators.
The Internal Revenue Service last July told states and localities that they can avoid enforcement action if they rebate yield burning profits that they made on refunding deals.
Issuers said such a plan would be unfair because underwriters, in most cases, kept hundreds of thousands of dollars in markups secret.
